critical.issue: _detect_energy_query() uses naive substring match: `kw in lower`. Short keyword 'pun' matches inside 'appuntamento' (and 'ipex' inside longer words, 'psv', etc.), causing false-positive Tavily calls on any message mentioning 'appuntamento'. Reproduced: message 'Qual è il mio prossimo appuntamento?' returns used_web_search=true with 5 governmental sources. Fix: use word-boundary regex or split into tokens.

action_items: Fix `_detect_energy_query()` in /app/backend/server.py:5514-5521 to use word-boundary matching (e.g., `re.search(r"\b(?:" + "|".join(map(re.escape,_ENERGY_KEYWORDS)) + r")\b", text.lower())`). Otherwise 'pun' inside 'appuntamento', 'appuntamenti', 'punto', 'oppure' (contains 'oneri'? no — but 'ttf' is safe; 'psv' matches 'psv…' words too) will keep triggering Tavily unnecessarily.
After fix, re-run `pytest backend/tests/test_v38t_neo_tavily_memory.py::TestTavilyWebSearch -v` to confirm the non-energy test passes.

rca_of_issue: Root cause of false-positive Tavily trigger: `_detect_energy_query(text)` uses `any(kw in lower for kw in _ENERGY_KEYWORDS)`. Since 'pun' is 3 letters and appears inside 'appuntamento' (positions 2-4: 'a-P-P-U-N-t-a-m-e-n-t-o' → substring 'pun' matches), any Italian sentence about appointments triggers a Tavily API call (wasting quota + adding ~10s latency) and marks the reply with used_web_search=true. Mitigation: replace substring check with `re.search(r'\b(pun|gme|mgp|gse|psv|ttf|ipex|spot|arera|arim|asos)\b', lower)` — word-boundary matching. Longer multi-word keywords like 'mercato elettrico', 'oneri di sistema' are safe as-is.
